title: Initial Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) Authentication Scheme Registrations
summary: Registers HTTP authentication schemes that were defined in RFCs before the IANA HTTP Authentication Scheme Registry existed, so the registry has an initial set of entries.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 7236 records the HTTP authentication schemes that existed before IANA created a registry for them. It gives each scheme a name and a reference to its specification.

questions: which http auth schemes are registered
what is the http authentication scheme registry
which authentication schemes are listed in rfc 7236
subtitle: The initial registrations in the HTTP authentication scheme registry.

tldr.problem: HTTP authentication schemes had been defined in RFCs before IANA established an HTTP Authentication Scheme Registry.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7236 registers the existing schemes and points each entry to the RFC that defines it.
tldr.outcome: The registry's initial entries are Basic, Bearer, Digest, Negotiate, and OAuth. The RFC says security considerations for each scheme belong in its defining specification.

today: RFC 7236 is an Informational document that records the initial entries in the HTTP Authentication Scheme Registry. It does not change the specifications for those authentication schemes.

sections.title: Why the Schemes Were Registered
sections.content: RFC 7236 registers HTTP authentication schemes that were defined in RFCs before the IANA HTTP Authentication Scheme Registry was established. The document is about recording those existing schemes in the registry, rather than defining their authentication behavior.
sections.plainLanguage: Several HTTP authentication schemes already had specifications. This RFC puts those names and specifications into one registry.

sections.title: The Initial Registry Entries
sections.content: The registry entries listed in RFC 7236 are Basic and Digest, referenced to RFC 2617; Bearer, referenced to RFC 6750; Negotiate, referenced to RFC 4559; and OAuth, referenced to RFC 5849. The registry table notes that Negotiate is connection-oriented and has syntax incompatible with the HTTP authentication header syntax.
sections.plainLanguage: The initial list contains Basic, Bearer, Digest, Negotiate, and OAuth. Each name points to the RFC that describes it.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states that the act of registering the schemes has no security considerations of its own. Security considerations that apply to an individual authentication scheme should be discussed in the specification that defines that scheme.
sections.plainLanguage: Adding the names to a registry does not change their security. Each scheme's own document covers its security issues.
